source: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for Diabetes Management in Chronic Kidney Disease
recommendations: Initiate first-line therapy with an SGLT2 inhibitor (if eGFR >= 20 mL/min/1.73m²)
Initiate RAS inhibitor (ACEi or ARB) titrated to maximum tolerated dose for hypertension/albuminuria
Prioritize lifestyle modifications: dietary sodium restriction < 2 g/day, physical activity
Avoid nephrotoxic agents including NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, and iodinated contrast if possible

follow_up.action: Initiate lifestyle modifications and assess baseline renal functions
Check serum creatinine and potassium after initiating ACEi/ARB or SGLT2 inhibitor
Comprehensive kidney evaluation: eGFR and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (uACR)

contraindications.action: Do not initiate therapy; discontinue if already taking unless kidney transplant patient

emergency_signs: Uremic symptoms: severe nausea, vomiting, metallic taste, progressive confusion
Hyperkalemia signs: muscle weakness, palpitations, or arrhythmias
Fluid overload: rapid weight gain, severe shortness of breath, severe peripheral edema
